en: *Samvarodayatantra*, Chapter 1: The Chapter on the Request (*Adhyeṣaṇāpaṭala*) Oṃ, homage to Herukavajra! Thus it was said: Oṃ, homage to Śrīvajrasattva! Oṃ, homage to Śrīhevajra! Thus have I heard at one time: the Blessed One was dwelling in the wombs (*bhaga*) of the Vajra Consorts of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas. Thereupon the Blessed One said: “The heart of the Lord, the heart of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, which is more secret than the secret—aho! Vajragarbha, well done, well done! O Great Compassionate One, Great Bodhisattva, listen to the heart of Vajrasattva, Mahāsattva, and Mahāsamayasattva, known as Hevajra. Vajragarbha said: “Why is he Vajrasattva? How is he Mahāsattva? By what is he Samayasattva? May the Blessed One tell me. The Blessed One said: “The indestructible is called *vajra*; the unity of the three realms of existence is *sattva*. One who is joined with this wisdom is known as Vajrasattva. [Chapter 1: The Chapter on the Request] Thus have I heard at one time: the Blessed One was dwelling in the wombs of the Vajra Yoginīs of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, amidst eighty million lords of yoga, headed by the noble Ānanda and others who had transcended passion, and foremost among them the noble Avalokiteśvara. Looking toward Vajrapāṇi, he smiled. Vajrapāṇi rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and with palms joined in reverence, made this request to the Blessed One: “I desire to hear, O Blessed One, the characteristics of the yoga of generation, And how, O God, is the yoga of completion, the single vow of all aspects? (1.1) How are wind, fire, water, earth, and space? O God, how are the five aspects, and from that, O Lord, the six sense objects? (1.2) How is the empowerment of the three bodies, situated externally and internally? Tell me, O Lord, the form of the deity and the goddess. (1.3) How are the moon and sun, O God, and how are the five paths? What is the nature of your body, and how is the form of the channels? (1.4) How is the attainment of the stages and so forth, and how is the vision of signs? How are your twelve activities, and how is the recitation of mantras? (1.5) What is the logic of the rosary, and what are the characteristics of recitation? What is the mandala-circle according to the yoga of the deity’s form? (1.6) Tell me, O Great Lord, the convention of signs and symbols; And how are the conventions of the sacred seats (*pīṭha*), both external and internal? (1.7) How is the mantra of accomplishment, O God, and how is the propitiation of Kaumārī? What should be performed during the day, and how is the offering of wine and food? (1.8) How are the five nectars and so forth, O God, and how are the five hooks? Tell me how the mandala is to be drawn, and how the laying of the lines is performed? (1.9) How is the purification of the site, and how is the protection wheel? By whom should the master be appointed, and how is the gathering of disciples? (1.10) What is the measure of the empowerments, and how is the fourth? What is the regulation of time, and how is the deception of death? (1.11) What are the four ages, and how do the four continents come to be? In each age, how is there accomplishment, and how is the conduct of the practitioner? (1.12) What is the Yoginī-tantra, and how does the Yoga-tantra come to be? What is the authority of the Sūtras, and what are the Perfections (*pāramitās*)? (1.13) How is the consecration, the fire sacrifice, and the yoga? How is the mantra of accomplishment, O God, and how is the elixir (*rasāyana*)? How is the drinking of wine? (1.14) How is the arising of the mantra, O God, and how is the extraction of the mantra? How is subjugation, O God, and how is grace, O Lord? (1.15) O Blessed One, how are the principles (*tattvas*), and how are emptiness and compassion? How is the nature of emptiness, and how is the essential nature of suchness? (1.16) What is the name of the divine form, the characteristics of the Yoginīs, and the offering? Tell me, O Lord, the full knowledge of all phenomena and their meditative cultivation. Thus ends the first chapter, the Chapter on the Request, of the glorious *Samvarodayatantra*.
